images.alt: Flow diagram of OSS Scanner: a maintainer's pull request, a human check, an online Docker build, an offline audit by Claude agents guided by the project's threat_model.md, then a proof of concept, patch and encrypted email with no 90-day disclosure clock
Column chart: over 29,000 candidate vulnerabilities found by Anthropic's models in six months, about 6,000 reviewed by humans, and nearly 5,000 sent unreviewed at maintainers' request

Screenshot of the threat_model.md template in Anthropic's oss-scanner repository on GitHub, with sections for where untrusted input enters, components that matter, how to exercise the code, how you rate severity, and anything to leave alone

caption: Maintainer tip: before an AI scanner touches your repo, write a threat_model.md that says where untrusted input enters and how you rate severity. OpenSSH and Valkey already did...
title: AI now finds the bugs for free. Your threat model decides whether that helps.
